source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Part 1 stores Arc<OperationSender<ServerT>> on QueuedEwsOperation and clones it from the client at enqueue. The queue and runners lose the sender and server generic; perform() uses the stored protocol sender, while a distinct oneshot sender reports the result. XpComEwsClient now calls sender shutdown after queue.stop().await. The historical stop closes submissions and clears runner handles without joining detached workers, so this ordered call is not proof of completed requests. The accepted source keeps per-operation sender ownership but uses a later external queue crate; that crate's completion behavior is not inferred here. The old trait comment still mentions a given OperationSender although perform has no sender argument. No Clippy, native or network result is claimed.
title: EWS sender ownership moves into each queued operation before queue extraction
